title: Challenger reward is 2% of owner-set price*size and is paid via notifyLoss even when the position has no debt: unbounded reserve drain / unbacked ZCHF mint
description: Lens B value-flow trace of end(): volume = price * size (price is a free, owner-controlled variable, only gated by a 3-day mint cooldown when raised), reward = 2% of volume, fundsNeeded = reward + repayment. If effectiveBid < fundsNeeded the hub calls zchf.notifyLoss(fundsNeeded - effectiveBid), which transfers the whole equity reserve and then MINTS the rest to the hub; the hub then pays the reward to the challenger. The reward does not depend on the position's minted debt (repayment = min(minted, volume) can be 0), on market value, or on the challenger being independent of the owner. Unlike DP1-1 (self-liquidation of a debt-carrying position), no debt, no vetted original and no dishonest bidder are needed: a clone with minimum collateral and _initialMint = 0 (no fee, no veto window) is enough. The attacker sets price to an astronomically high value, a second address launches a challenge of size s >= minimumCollateral with its own collateral, nobody can avert (averting requires bid >= price*s), and after challengePeriod end() pays the challenger 2%*price*s out of the reserve and then out of newly minted ZCHF. The challenger's collateral is returned, and the position's collateral goes to the end() caller, so the attacker's cost is only gas plus temporary collateral.
root_cause: Reward and loss coverage are denominated in a position parameter the owner can set arbitrarily high at any time (adjustPrice has no upper bound or collateral-value check when raising), and notifyLoss will mint unlimited ZCHF once the reserve is exhausted; there is no cap relative to minted debt, realised bid or collateral value.
recommendation: Cap the reward by realised value (e.g. min(reward, bid-based or debt-based amount)), do not let price-derived quantities drive notifyLoss, and bound/validate upward price changes.

harm.who: FPS holders (equity reserve), minter reserve, and all ZCHF holders via inflation
harm.loses_what: entire ZCHF reserve and then unbounded newly minted unbacked ZCHF
harm.magnitude: 2% * price * size, with price attacker-chosen: effectively unbounded (limited only by uint256 overflow of price*size)

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker calls MintingHub.clonePosition(vettedPosition, minCollateral, 0): gets a clone with price 0, minted 0, no veto window, no fee.
2. Attacker calls clone.adjustPrice(1e45) (increase path: no collateral check, only 3-day mint cooldown, no challenge active).
3. A second address calls launchChallenge(clone, s) with s >= minimumCollateral; averting would require a bid >= price*s, so nobody bids.
4. After challengePeriod anyone calls end(n): volume = price*s, repayment = 0, reward = 2%*volume, effectiveBid = 0, hub calls notifyLoss(reward): reserve is drained, remainder is minted to the hub.
5. Hub transfers reward to the challenger; challenger collateral is returned; the end() caller receives the position collateral. Attacker holds the minted ZCHF and can repeat.

preconditions.text: attacker can clone any position that is alive, unchallenged and out of cooldown (or open its own position and avoid veto)
no honest party pays price*size to avert (impossible for large price)

postconditions.text: equity reserve reduced to 0 and unbacked ZCHF minted to challenger

title: Owner can raise the liquidation price at any time (only a 3-day cooldown) and clones skip the veto window, allowing unbacked minting up to the limit
description: Discovery: Q3.1 / Q1.4 (sufficiency of the check). Governance's only protection against a bad price is the veto during the first 3 days (Position.deny, start check). adjustPrice() allows increasing the price without any collateral check or governance hook; it only triggers restrictMinting(3 days). A clone is created without veto window (cooldown storage starts at 0, no OPENING_FEE) and gets price = _mint*1e18/_coll, which is 0 for _mint = 0; the clone owner can then raise the price arbitrarily. After 3 days the owner mints up to the clone's limit against dust collateral.
root_cause: The price used by checkCollateral() is fully owner-controlled after the veto period, so the collateral invariant 'collateral * price >= minted' can be made trivially true; vetting by governance applies only at position creation, not to later price changes or clones.

harm.magnitude: up to the limit given to the clone (half of the remaining limit of the original) or the original's limit

title: Zero/dust bids are always accepted and extend the challenge by 30 minutes, letting anyone stall a liquidation indefinitely at gas cost
description: Discovery: Q-attacker on bid() / lending-liquidation-deep (auction gaming), deepening DP1-3. With no prior bid, minBid() = 0*1005/1000 = 0, so bid(n, 0, size) passes the BidTooLow check, sets bidder = msg.sender, transfers 0 ZCHF and, when called inside the last 30 minutes, bumps challenge.end to now + 30 minutes. Because challenge.bid stays 0 the minimum never grows, so the same call can be repeated every <30 minutes forever. Below 200 wei, floor(bid*1.005) == bid, so a 1 wei bid has the same property. end() requires block.timestamp >= challenge.end, so the challenge can never be settled, the position stays under challengedAmount > 0 (mint, withdraw and adjustPrice all revert), and the challenger's collateral is locked in the hub. The 0-bidder is additionally set as recipient of the position collateral in end(), displacing the end() caller.
root_cause: bid() does not require a strictly positive, strictly increasing bid when challenge.bid == 0 and applies the ebay-style time extension to such bids; the anti-stall argument in the code comment (0.5% per 30 minutes) only holds for bid > 200 wei.

harm.who: challengers (locked collateral, no reward) and the protocol (undercollateralised position cannot be liquidated)
harm.loses_what: liveness of liquidation; challenger collateral locked for as long as the attacker keeps bidding; bad debt accrues against the reserve
harm.magnitude: the whole challenge size plus the position's debt, for the price of about 48 cheap txs per day

exploit_trace: 1. Challenger calls launchChallenge(pos, size); the position is overpriced or undercollateralised so nobody would pay price*size.

2. The position owner (or any griefer) calls bid(n, 0, size) when 29 minutes remain: tryAvertChallenge(size, 0) returns false, minBid == 0 so no revert, challenge.end = now + 30 minutes, bidder = attacker, bid = 0.
3. 29 minutes later the attacker calls bid(n, 0, size) again; minBid is still 0, end is pushed again.
4. end(n) always reverts with 'period has not ended'; the challenger cannot recover collateral or settle, the position stays locked and the bad debt is never liquidated.

preconditions.text: no honest bidder has placed a bid above ~200 wei (a real bid raises minBid by 0.5% per round and costs the staller real funds)

postconditions.text: challenge never settles; position permanently under challengedAmount > 0

title: Costless launchChallenge + self-avert bid re-arms the 1-day mint/withdraw cooldown on any position, locking the owner's collateral and blocking cloning indefinitely
description: Discovery: MODIFIER-01 / state-transition check (who may trigger restrictMinting). launchChallenge is permissionless, and bid() lets the challenger himself be the averting bidder: tryAvertChallenge only checks bid*1e18 >= price*size and then calls restrictMinting(1 days) on the position. In the averted path bid() pays the bid to challenge.challenger and returns the collateral to msg.sender, so when challenger == bidder both legs net to zero. The attacker pays only gas (and needs price*size ZCHF / size collateral for the duration of the two calls). Each round sets cooldown = now + 1 day on the position, and while the challenge is open challengedAmount > 0 as well. withdrawCollateral, mint and reduceLimitForClone (hence clonePosition) all require noCooldown (and noChallenge), so repeating once per day keeps the owner from withdrawing collateral or minting and prevents anybody from cloning the position, until the position expires (tryAvertChallenge returns false after expiration).
root_cause: A costless, permissionless action (challenge then self-avert) is allowed to extend a cooldown that guards the owner's core operations. Nothing prevents the challenger from being the averting bidder and the cooldown extension is not conditional on the bid being paid by a third party or costing the averting party anything.

harm.loses_what: access to their collateral (withdraw/repay-then-withdraw) and minting capacity for as long as the attack is sustained
harm.magnitude: whole collateral of any non-expired position can be frozen until expiration at gas cost only

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker holds minimumCollateral of the position's collateral token and price*minimumCollateral ZCHF (both recovered at the end).
2. Attacker calls MintingHub.launchChallenge(pos, minimumCollateral): challengedAmount > 0, owner cannot mint, adjustPrice or withdrawCollateral for the challenge duration.

3. Just before challenge.end attacker calls bid(n, price*size/1e18 rounded up, size): tryAvertChallenge returns true, restrictMinting(1 days) sets cooldown = now + 1 day; ZCHF goes to himself, collateral returns to himself.
4. Attacker immediately repeats from step 2; the owner is never outside challenge or cooldown, cannot withdraw collateral or mint, and clonePosition reverts with Hot().
5. Result: owner's collateral frozen until expiration at attacker cost of gas only.

preconditions.text: attacker can temporarily hold price*size ZCHF and size collateral (size >= minimumCollateral)

postconditions.text: owner and cloners locked out of withdraw/mint/clone for the lifetime of the position

title: Zero-mint clones each take half of the remaining limit of a position (limit stealing / griefing)
description: Discovery: Q5.3 (called repeatedly) / Q3.1. clonePosition is permissionless and charges no fee. title: While ZCHF totalSupply is 0, anyone can register themselves as an immediately active minter (no fee, no application period) and mint unlimited ZCHF
description: Discovery: AC-01 / bootstrap edge case (what if totalSupply == 0). The minimum application period and minimum fee are only enforced when totalSupply() > 0 (to let the deployer register the first minter). suggestMinter is permissionless, so before the first ZCHF exists any address can call suggestMinter(attacker, 0, 0, ""): minters[attacker] = block.timestamp, and isMinter is true when block.timestamp >= minters[_minter], i.e. immediately. denyMinter reverts TooLate as soon as block.timestamp > minters[_minter] and in any case Equity has no votes yet. The attacker then calls mint(attacker, type(uint128).max) via the minterOnly path.
root_cause: The bootstrap exception for the first minter is available to every caller, not only the deployer, and the minter set is irrevocable once the application period (here 0) has elapsed.

harm.who: the protocol deployer and every later ZCHF user
harm.loses_what: the deployment is compromised from block one: attacker holds unlimited mint power over ZCHF (also able to squat the bridge/hub addresses first)

exploit_trace: 1. Frankencoin is deployed; totalSupply() == 0 until the deployer registers and uses the first minter.
2. Attacker front-runs or simply acts in the gap and calls suggestMinter(attacker, 0, 0, "x").
3. minters[attacker] = block.timestamp, so isMinter(attacker) is true in the same or next block; nobody can deny it (TooLate; Equity has no FPS).

4. Attacker calls mint(attacker, hugeAmount) and registerPosition for arbitrary addresses; the deployer's later suggestMinter for the hub reverts only if the attacker took that address (AlreadyRegistered).
5. Deployer must redeploy; if value was already bridged in, the ZCHF is worthless.

preconditions.text: ZCHF totalSupply() == 0 (between deployment and first mint)

postconditions.text: attacker is a permanent minter; minters cannot be removed after the application window

title: checkQualified passes for any caller when totalVotes() is 0 (no FPS yet, or same block as first mint), letting anyone veto minters and positions
description: Discovery: GOV-01 zero-supply variant. The quorum test is _votes * 10000 < QUORUM * totalVotes(). When totalVotes() == 0 the right side is 0 and the test never reverts, even for a caller with zero votes and no helpers. totalVotes() is 0 while no FPS exist (FPS can only be minted once equity >= 1000 ZCHF) and in the block in which the first FPS is minted (votes accrue per block). During that window anyone can call Frankencoin.denyMinter(_minter, [], msg) on every pending minter application and Position.deny([], msg) on every position still in its init period, cancelling them at zero cost. The same hole lets anyone call Equity.restructureCapTable with zero votes whenever equity < 1000 and supply is 0 (also after every FPS was wiped).
root_cause: Quorum is a percentage of a live total that is allowed to be zero, with no minimum absolute vote requirement or non-zero check.
vulnerable_code:
uint256 _votes = votes(sender, helpers);
if (_votes * 10000 < QUORUM * totalVotes()) revert NotQualified();

title: Any caller of end() can force postponeCollateralReturn=true, parking the challenger's collateral in pendingReturns
description: Discovery: MODIFIER-01 (parameter meant for the challenger is controlled by an arbitrary caller). end(n, postpone) is permissionless and the documented purpose of postpone is a blacklisted challenger, but the flag is chosen by whoever calls end. A third party (who also receives the position collateral when there is no bidder) can set postpone = true, so the challenger's own collateral is credited to pendingReturns[collateral][challenger] instead of being sent. title: FPS minted for dust when total supply is below 1000 FPS: calculateSharesInternal ignores the invested amount
description: calculateSharesInternal returns newTotalShares - totalShares where newTotalShares = 1000e18 whenever totalSupply() < 1000e18, regardless of capitalBefore and investment. If the FPS supply ever falls below 1000 shares (the initial depositor receives exactly 1000 FPS and can redeem any part of it after the holding period; redeem only requires shares + 1e18 < totalSupply) while equity is positive, the next caller who sends any amount that keeps equity() >= MINIMUM_EQUITY (even 1 wei, since the existing equity already satisfies the requirement) receives 1000e18 - totalSupply new shares, i.e. a majority of the pool, at no real cost. After the holding period these shares redeem for the corresponding fraction of the existing equity. A related boundary: when capitalBefore <= 0 (equity <= amount) a fixed 1000 FPS is issued independent of the existing supply, so a recapitaliser into a negative-equity pool with large supply receives a negligible share (relies on restructureCapTable).
root_cause: Bootstrap special case keyed on totalSupply rather than on capital: share issuance is not a function of the amount paid when supply < 1000 FPS.
recommendation: Apply the fixed 1000-share bootstrap only when capitalBefore is 0 (or supply is 0); otherwise use the bonding curve.
vulnerable_code:
uint256 newTotalShares = totalShares < 1000 * ONE_DEC18 ? 1000 * ONE_DEC18 : _mulD18(totalShares, _cubicRoot(_divD18(capitalBefore + investment, capitalBefore)));
return newTotalShares - totalShares;

harm.loses_what: most of the equity value through dilution
harm.magnitude: up to (1000 - supply)/1000 of equity per exploit

exploit_trace: 1. Initial depositor holds 1000 FPS and redeems e.g. 500 after the 90-day holding period; supply = 500 FPS, equity still E (> 1000 ZCHF).
2. Attacker calls zchf.transferAndCall(equity, 1 wei, '') (equity() after transfer >= 1000 ZCHF holds from existing balance).

4. After the holding period the attacker redeems and receives about 87.5% of the capital via the cubic curve for 50% of shares (or votes with 50%).

postconditions.text: attacker owns a large FPS fraction for dust

title: Partial challenge clears the owner's whole debt because repayment is min(minted, price*size) rather than proportional to the challenged share
description: The code comment argues volume >= minted*size/colBal, so the repayment is at least proportional. But the repayment is capped only by minted, not by the proportional share. For a position with collateral C, minted M and price P with P*C >> M, a challenge of size s with P*s >= M burns the entire debt M while only s of C collateral is sold at the (market-value) bid. The owner keeps C - s collateral debt-free; the difference between M + reward and the bid is covered by notifyLoss (reserve or newly minted ZCHF). The owner (or colluding challenger) can engineer this by raising price, then self-challenging a slice of the collateral.
root_cause: Debt forgiveness is computed from the owner-controlled price instead of the proportional share minted * size / collateralBalance.
recommendation: Cap repayment at minted * size / collateralBalance (rounded up) or tie it to the realised bid.

harm.who: reserve / FPS holders and ZCHF holders
harm.loses_what: reserve ZCHF equal to debt not backed by the sold slice of collateral
harm.magnitude: up to minted per challenge sequence

exploit_trace: 1. Owner holds C=100 collateral, minted M=500, price P=10 (market 8); a slice s=60 gives volume 600 >= M.
2. Challenge on s=60 ends with bid 480 (market value) or none.
3. repayment = 500 (all debt), reward = 12, bid 480 < 512: notifyLoss(32+).
4. Owner keeps the remaining 40 collateral with zero debt and the unspent minted ZCHF.

title: bid() and end() make collateral transfers to the caller/challenger before the challenge is deleted (CEI violation), enabling double refund / double return with a callback collateral token
description: Discovery: RE-01 / CALLBACK-01 / HOOK-01, Module A (untrusted recipient) and Module C (transfer order). Positions accept any ERC20 as collateral and the hub does not restrict token behaviour. In end(), returnCollateral() transfers the challenger's collateral to the challenger (an arbitrary address) before notifyChallengeSucceeded() and before `delete challenges[...]`. A recipient reachable by a transfer hook (ERC777-style tokensReceived, ERC1363) can re-enter end() for the same challenge: the challenge is still stored, so the collateral is returned a second time out of the hub's pooled balance for that token (other challengers' deposits) and the settlement runs twice. In bid(), the averted branch calls collateral.transfer(msg.sender, size) before `delete challenges[...]` while challenge.bid and challenge.bidder still hold the previous bid, so a re-entrant bid() refunds the old bid a second time from the hub's pooled ZCHF.
root_cause: State (challenge struct, challengedAmount, bid) is cleared only after external token transfers; there is no reentrancy guard, and the hub holds collateral and ZCHF for many challenges in one pooled balance.

harm.who: other challengers and bidders whose collateral/bids sit in the hub
harm.loses_what: pooled collateral of the hook token and pooled ZCHF bids
harm.magnitude: one extra challenge.size of collateral or one extra old bid per re-entry

exploit_trace: 1. Attacker opens a position whose collateral is a callback-capable token; other users have open challenges holding the same token (or ZCHF bids) in the hub.
2. Attacker contract launches a challenge; after the period, anyone calls end(n).
3. returnCollateral transfers size to the attacker contract; its hook calls hub.end(n) again before delete.

4. The nested call returns size again from the pooled balance and runs notifyChallengeSucceeded; the outer call then continues, double-spending hub-held assets of other challenges (the second settlement only reverts if no other challenge exists on the position).

title: Permissionless splitChallenge front-runs bids and invalidates expectedSize, letting a griefer stall bidders on a challenge it wants to succeed
description: Discovery: Module N (DoS-to-exploit escalation) / Module T shared-state mutation order. splitChallenge has no access control and no time limit: any address can split any open challenge, and each split changes challenge.size. bid() reverts with UnexpectedSize whenever expectedSize != challenge.size. An attacker that benefits from a challenge succeeding unaverted (the owner/challenger pair of DC-2/DP1-1) watches the mempool and front-runs every bid(n, x, size) with splitChallenge(n, minimumCollateral), so the bid reverts; the bidder must re-read and resend, and the attacker repeats while size >= 2*minimumCollateral (position owners choose minimumCollateral, which can be 1 wei). Splitting also pro-rates bids, fragmenting a prior bid.
root_cause: splitChallenge is callable by anyone, at any time, with no cost, and bid() binds to the exact current size.

harm.who: bidders attempting to avert a challenge, and the position owner if third parties are blocked
harm.loses_what: ability to avert a challenge before it ends; the collateral of the challenged position
harm.magnitude: the challenged collateral, if the attacker can out-race bidders until the period ends

2. A bidder broadcasts bid(n, price*S, S).
3. Attacker front-runs with splitChallenge(n, min): challenge.size becomes S-min.
4. The bid reverts with UnexpectedSize. Attacker repeats for each resubmission until the challenge ends, then calls end().

title: Owner can raise price to a value that overflows price*size, making bid() and end() revert forever: position becomes unliquidatable and challenger collateral is stuck in the hub
description: Parameter MAX test on price. adjustPrice() has no upper bound when the price is raised (only a 3 day mint cooldown, no collateral check). Both liquidation paths multiply price by a challenge size with checked arithmetic: tryAvertChallenge computes `price * _collateralAmount` (bid path) and notifyChallengeSucceeded computes `_mulD18(price,_size)` = price*_size/1e18 (end path). For price > 2^256/size (e.g. type(uint256).max) both revert with a Panic. Hence launchChallenge (which does not touch price) still takes the challenger's collateral into the hub, but the challenge can neither be averted (bid reverts) nor ended (end reverts, and the whole tx including returnCollateral rolls back). The challenger's collateral is permanently stuck and the position can never be liquidated, regardless of how far the collateral value falls. An owner that has minted against the collateral can front-run any pending launchChallenge (noChallenge is only checked at execution) or set the price preemptively once the veto window is over.
root_cause: Unbounded owner-controlled price combined with unchecked-range multiplications on the liquidation path; no sanity bound on price at adjustPrice and no fallback when volume cannot be computed.
recommendation: Bound price at adjustPrice (and in checkCollateral/constructor) so price * maxChallengeSize cannot overflow, or use mulDiv/saturating arithmetic in the liquidation path.

harm.who: Challengers (stuck collateral) and ZCHF holders / FPS reserve (undliquidatable bad debt)
harm.loses_what: challenger collateral locked in MintingHub forever; minted ZCHF of the position can never be recovered via liquidation
harm.magnitude: entire minted amount of the position plus any collateral posted by challengers

exploit_trace: 1. Owner mints M ZCHF against collateral C at a vetted price.
2. After the veto window, owner calls adjustPrice(type(uint256).max) (allowed: no collateral check on increase).
3. Collateral value drops; challenger calls launchChallenge(position,size) and deposits size tokens into the hub.
4. bid(): tryAvertChallenge reverts on price*size overflow; end(): notifyChallengeSucceeded reverts on _mulD18 overflow.
5. Challenge can never be resolved: challenger's tokens are stuck, position never liquidated, loss accumulates in the system.

preconditions.text: no active challenge when owner raises the price, veto window over

postconditions.text: position unliquidatable; challenger collateral locked in hub

title: initializeClone floors the clone price, so checkCollateral fails for every _mint not divisible in the collateral ratio (clone creation reverts)
description: Mechanical trace: _coll=3e18, _mint=1e18. price = 1e18*1e18/3e18 = 333333333333333333 (floor). mintInternal -> checkCollateral(3e18, price): 3e18*333333333333333333 = 999999999999999999e18 < 1e18*1e18 -> InsufficientCollateral. The check passes only if _mint*1e18 % _coll == 0 (or _mint = 0). clonePosition therefore reverts for most amounts; users must pre-compute a divisible pair. For _mint = 0 the price becomes 0 (no minting but price can be raised later, see DP1-2).
root_cause: Price derived by rounding down and then re-checked against the exact invariant.

harm.loses_what: failed transactions / unusable clone path for non-divisible parameters
